answer: The velvet multiplier is published, charged in reef, and fable lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4110 identities would post 3470 proofs and burn roughly 75 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
